item.title: Australia Gets States’ Buy-in for AI Data Center Energy Rules
item.description: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said he has secured agreement from regional leaders — including from holdout state Queensland — to press on with new rules on AI data centers’ energy use by next year.
item.dc:creator: Kristine Servando

item.title: Xi to Make First Egypt Trip in Decade, Attend Kyrgyzstan Summit
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping will visit Egypt for the first time in a decade, extending a trip that will also take him to a regional security summit in Kyrgyzstan.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Indian Student Unrest Persists in Challenge to Modi’s Government
item.description: Student protests continue to simmer across India, a month after nationwide demonstrations over an exam scandal forced the country’s education minister to resign, underscoring persistent anger over the integrity of the country’s testing and recruitment system.
item.dc:creator: Atul Dev

item.title: Iran and Oman Discuss Strait of Hormuz Deal | Daybreak Europe 8/26/2026
item.description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and his Omani counterpart Badr Albusaidi discussed an “interim framework” aimed at resuming shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, according to a joint statement carried by the Oman News Agency, as the two sides press ahead with long-running talks over navigation through the key waterway.
Stocks rose as Asian chipmakers advanced ahead of Nvidia results, with traders looking to the chip bellwether’s earnings for the next beat in the AI trade.
And the Trump administration is discussing additional trade penalties against Canada after PM Mark Carney unveiled dollar-for-dollar retaliation to new US tariffs. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Pick Darline Graham Wins South Carolina Senate Runoff
item.description: Senator Darline Graham prevailed in a Republican runoff to replace her late brother Lindsey Graham as the GOP candidate in South Carolina’s US Senate race, a victory aided by heavy support from President Donald Trump. Bloomberg's Jon Herskovitz has more. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Administration Prepares Next Move as Canada Trade War Spirals
item.description: The Trump administration is discussing additional trade penalties against Canada after Prime Minister Mark Carney unveiled dollar-for-dollar retaliation to new tariffs imposed by the US. The threat underscores the prospect of a spiraling trade war between the two nations. Bloomberg's Jill Disis breaks down the situation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Iran, Oman Discuss 'Interim' Reopening of Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and his Omani counterpart Badr Albusaidi discussed an “interim framework” aimed at resuming shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, according to a joint statement carried by the Oman News Agency. Bloomberg's Abeer Abu Omar has the latest. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Russia’s Escalating Hybrid Attacks Put Europeans in a Bind
item.description: Russia is expanding its campaign of hybrid attacks against countries that supply weapons and money to Kyiv and has caught Europe without a plan to respond.
item.dc:creator: Aaron Eglitis and Milda Seputyte

item.title: Orban’s EU Influence Comes to an Abrupt End as Cash Dries Up
item.description: Viktor Orban’s power network in his home country isn’t the only one being dismantled — a political operation the former Hungarian leader spent years building in Brussels is also coming undone.
item.dc:creator: Yurii Stasiuk

item.title: Mass Border Breach Exposes Deep Divisions in Spain’s African Exclave Ceuta
item.description: Julián Domínguez has been a doctor in Ceuta for nearly four decades.

item.description: The Trump administration is discussing additional trade penalties against Canada after Prime Minister Mark Carney unveiled dollar-for-dollar retaliation to new tariffs imposed by the US. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: China Renews Scrutiny of Military Procurement With Call for Tips
item.description: China’s military is asking the public to report suspected violations in the Rocket Force, extending scrutiny of a branch at the center of President Xi Jinping’s shake-up of the armed forces.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Bolivia’s Paz Names Morales as New Finance Chief With New Loans a Priority
item.description: Bolivia’s President Rodrigo Paz named Christian Andrés Morales as his new finance minister with a charge to work with international lenders to secure as much as $10 billion in new financing.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Mendoza

item.title: Trump-Backed Darline Graham Wins Senate Runoff in South Carolina
item.description: Senator Darline Graham prevailed in a Republican runoff to replace her late brother Lindsey Graham as the GOP candidate in South Carolina’s US Senate race, a victory aided by heavy support from President Donald Trump.

item.title: Canada Doubles Tariffs on US Steel Products up to 50% | Balance of Power: Late Edition 08/25/2026
item.description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Ontario Premier Doug Ford says Canada should answer US tariffs “tariff for tariff and dollar for dollar,” but urges President Donald Trump and Prime Minister Mark Carney to reach a fair agreement. Sen. Ted Cruz (R-TX) says tariff threats should be used to open markets, lower trade barriers and expand trade—not to keep tariffs high indefinitely. Michael Faulkender, Former Deputy Secretary of the United States Treasury, says Kevin Warsh should reinforce his commitment to bringing inflation back to 2.0%, while arguing that energy-driven price pressures do not justify an interest-rate increase. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Weighs More Trade Measures Against Canada After Retaliation
item.description: The Trump administration is discussing additional trade penalties against Canada after Prime Minister Mark Carney unveiled dollar-for-dollar retaliation to new tariffs imposed by the US on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Mason

item.title: Ugandan President’s Son Declares Bid to Succeed His Father
item.description: The son of long-serving Uganda President Yoweri Museveni said he plans to succeed his father in the country’s next elections.
item.dc:creator: Simon Marks

item.title: Imran Khan’s Life Is At Risk In Pakistan Prison, Sons Say
item.description: Former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan’s life is at risk due to the conditions of his prison confinement, his sons said during an emotional news conference on Tuesday, adding that efforts to visit their jailed father have hit a wall.
item.dc:creator: Tooba Khan, Bilal Hussain (News) and Dan Strumpf

item.title: China, India Border Talks Signal Progress Before Likely Xi Visit
item.description: China and India agreed to pursue settlement of their border dispute in the latest round of high-level talks this week, as both sides lay the groundwork for a possible visit by President Xi Jinping to New Delhi next month.
item.dc:creator: Sudhi Ranjan Sen and Jing Li

item.title: Xi Signals Defiance as US Threatens Sanctions Over Iran Help
item.description: Xi Jinping’s government is sending a message of defiance to Donald Trump over China’s economic ties with Iran.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News
